# South Africa

The wealth gradients this library holds for South Africa: first the values to give OG-Core, then the measurements behind them. New to the terms? See the [glossary](../glossary.md).

## What to use in OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Tilt | From |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | **by age**, table below (fertility tilt −0.51 plus the [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md)) | DHS 2016 |
| `infmort_gradient` | **−0.54** | DHS 2016 |
| `mort_gradient` | **−0.80** (ages 15–60) | census 2011, own measurement |
| `imm_pctiles` | not covered by this library | — |

Every value is a **tilt** ([what that is](../glossary.md#tilt)). Convert it before passing it to OG-Core: `tilt / (100 × (1 − p))`, with p OG-Core's own rate at that age ([how](../methods/ogcore-units.md)).

**Fertility tilt by mother's age** (for `fert_gradient`; ages under 15 take the 15–19 value, 50 and over the 45–49 value):

| 15–19 | 20–24 | 25–29 | 30–34 | 35–39 | 40–44 | 45–49 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| −1.28 | −0.60 | −0.30 | −0.18 | −0.41 | −0.90 | −1.49 |

> **Note.** The 2011 census links only 9% of deaths to household assets: the tilt is usable, the death-rate levels are not.

## Where these numbers come from

### Household surveys (DHS)

Latest survey, from [`data/gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv). Earlier surveys are in `gradient_library.csv`.

| Measure | Survey | Tilt | Poorest ÷ richest tenth | Poorest fifth → richest fifth |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Births per woman (TFR) | 2016 | **−0.51** | 1.5× | 3.1 · 2.9 · 2.7 · 2.3 · 2.1 |
| Infant deaths per 1,000 births (IMR) | 2016 | **−0.54** | 1.4× | 54 · 44 · 46 · 27 · 40 |
| Under-5 deaths per 1,000 births (U5MR) | 2016 | **−0.70** | 1.6× | 67 · 52 · 51 · 34 · 41 |

| Census | Ages 15–60 | 15–29 | 30–44 | 45–59 | 60–74 | Wealth groups | Deaths |

| 2001 | **−0.79** | −0.92 | −1.17 | −0.86 | −0.32 | 5 | 20,193 |

## Notes

- Three censuses (2001, 2007, 2011) plus DHS 2016. The 2011 census links only ~9% of death records to asset data (`linked_share`), so its *levels* are meaningless — but the linked deaths match the unlinked on province, urban/rural, sex, and age, so the tilt is unbiased.
- A per-sample lesson recorded in the pipeline: IPUMS `AUTOS` code 7 means "has a car, count unspecified", not seven cars; treating it as a count materially changed the 2011 tilt (−1.14 → −0.80).
- The DHS 2016 child-mortality quintile cells are visibly noisy (non-monotonic top quintiles) — small death counts in a low-mortality survey. The tilt is usable; individual cells are not.
- South Africa's own census measurement (−0.80) should be used over the general gradient's prediction (−0.83).
